notation.description: Directions assume your character faces right. Mirror them when facing left.

Down-back; 1 in numpad notation when facing right

Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3 Super Art / Punish Counter

Next action in order; timing and cancel rules are only specified when explicitly annotated

notationLegend.meaning: Instant air teleport; follow the demonstrated airborne timing
Yoga Teleport / Yoga Float; follow each reference's movement and timing notes
Denjin Renki. Each reference states when a stored charge is required.
Tatsumaki Senpukyaku / its airborne version; strength and timing follow the reference.
Shoryuken; L, M, H and OD identify the demonstrated version.
High Blade Kick (Jodan Sokutogeri). These names refer to the same special move.
Hashogeki. Denjin versions require a stored charge when stated in the reference.
Tatsumaki Zanku-kyaku; strength and timing follow the reference.
Gou Shoryuken; L, M, H and OD identify the demonstrated version.
Gou Hadoken / Zanku Hadoken. Charged versions are identified in the reference.
Adamant Flame is Akuma's quarter-circle-back punch special. A ~ marks a follow-up action; use the listed button and timing.
Demon Raid (Hyakkishu). Each reference identifies the demonstrated follow-up or landing action.
Conditions state any required medal level. Match that starting state before practising.
Manon's command throw, distinct from the Renversé hit grab. Use the listed strength.
Renversé, the striking special that leads into its throw. Follow the reference's version and execution cues.
Rond-point; L, M, H and OD identify the demonstrated version.
Dégagé; follow the strength and spacing stated in each reference.
Serenity Stream. Entering the stance and pressing a follow-up button are separate actions; follow the listed continuation or exit.
Down-forward heavy punch, Chun-Li’s overhead. This is distinct from SS.HP, the heavy-punch follow-up from Serenity Stream.
Spinning Bird Kick. Brackets such as [2] mean hold that direction before completing the input. Follow each reference’s charge or stance execution cue.
Hundred Lightning Kicks / Aerial Hundred Lightning Kicks. Use the listed strength and grounded or airborne version.
Tensho Kicks, distinct from Spinning Bird Kick. Use the listed strength.
Yosokyaku, the airborne down-medium-kick stomp. Follow the demonstrated jump direction and number of stomps.
Chun-Li’s projectile. Follow the strength and charge or stance execution cue stated in the reference.
Brackets mean hold the direction before completing the input. [4] is back charge; [2] is down charge. Follow each reference’s charge and release cues.
Guile’s charged projectile. Use the listed strength and any Perfect execution cue stated in the reference.
These names refer to the same down-charge kick. Use the listed strength and preserve charge during the preceding actions.
Sonic Blade places a stationary projectile. Sonic Cross is the projectile continuation after Blade; follow the listed strength, input and timing.
Solid Puncher is Guile’s Level 2 Super Art. Sonic Break actions during it are separate follow-ups; match the listed buttons and timing.
Back heavy punch can appear as a separate link or as the medium-punch target follow-up. Match the reference’s timing cue; these are different routes.
Down-forward heavy kick (3HK) and crouching heavy punch (2HP) are different attacks. Match the listed standing or crouching opponent condition.
Heavy-punch and medium-punch Sonic Hurricane. Use the listed punch version; a launcher and its juggle continuation are not interchangeable.
Use the listed punch strength. Perfect means release at the demonstrated charge timing; a regular release is not interchangeable.
Airborne light Flash Knuckle with the demonstrated partial hold, after the jumping-medium-punch juggle.
The standing-medium-punch target sequence. Later presses are target continuations, not repeated linked standing medium punches.
Rising Uppercut / Sand Blast. Use the listed strength.
Jamie’s current drink level. Match each reference’s shown starting state; some target routes and airborne specials require unlocked moves.
The manual drink action. It is separate from Arrow Kick, and can give the opponent time to recover.
The drink-level-1 light target sequence. Later buttons are target continuations.
Crouching-heavy-kick target route, including its heavy-kick continuation and final drinking punch continuation.
Down plus two kick buttons for the shown launcher; jump-cancel it before the airborne heavy kick.
Target continuations. The later presses continue the target route, rather than linking separate standing normals.
Sprint into the listed punch or kick branch. The punch branch stops the run; the demonstrated kick branches are distinct and are not interchangeable.
The run step from contact into the airborne kick continuation. Keep the shown corner spacing and OD versus normal run distinction.
Heavy Vagabond Edge launch / regular airborne grab / OD airborne grab. Use the grounded launch before the airborne input.
Medium bomb placement. Requires an available spray can and creates a later timing situation, not an immediate combo hit.
Juri’s stored resource. OD Fuhajin adds one stock; enhanced Go Ohsatsu and its enhanced Ankensatsu continuation each spend one. Check the entry’s starting-stock requirement.
Forward medium punch / back heavy kick. They are distinct post-launch normals with different spacing and knockdown results.
Enhanced Go Ohsatsu followed by the enhanced Ankensatsu continuation. MK is the special follow-up, not a standing medium kick.
Critical Art version of Level 3, requiring the appropriate low-health state as well as three Super stocks.
Quick Dash uses two kicks. LK during the run stops it; this is distinct from a forward dash and from Drive Rush.
Standing medium punch followed by its heavy-punch target continuation.

notationLegend.term: Run DP / Run Tatsu / Run Dragonlash
notationLegend.meaning: The demonstrated punch, quarter-circle-back kick, or dragon-punch-motion kick continuation during Quick Dash.
Hold back for Rolling Attack or down for Vertical Rolling Attack before the release.
Down plus two punches enters the low stance. The subsequent P is Wild Lift, a separate launching action.
An aerial charge special; preserve the listed direction and button strength through the preceding juggle.
Hold back or down before releasing the listed charge special. Build charge during the preceding actions.
The dash has separate punch follow-ups. 2P is Taiho Cannon Lift; P then P is the two-stage Teppo Triple Slap.
Down-forward heavy kick is the overhead stomp. It is different from the crouching heavy kick.
Double down plus punch is the clap. The creator’s “Sumo Spirit” note beside Hands identifies the empowered Hands state.
A stocked Sumo Spirit changes Hundred Hand Slap. Preserve the stocked-state prerequisite in empowered routes.
63214K is the half-circle-back command throw. A throw after blockstun or wake-up is a pressure attempt, not a combo.
Hold down before up plus the listed kick for Jackknife Maximum. Double-Jackknife routes require recharging between versions.
Medium Double Rolling Sobat is the forward quarter-circle kick used in these knockdown setups.
Quarter-circle back plus the listed punch. The medium and heavy routes are distinct from Jackknife enders.
The medium-medium-heavy sequence is a target combo. Match the follow-up timing rather than treating it as three independent normal links.
Dimachaerus followed by its forward-punch continuation. The follow-up is part of the special sequence.
Target continuation, rather than a link between separate standing attacks.
Fully hold the stated attack button as demonstrated. A held normal and an unheld normal can create different launch and juggle states.
OD Quadriga / OD Phalanx. These spend Drive and are not interchangeable with their regular versions.
Back heavy punch / forward medium punch, relative to the opponent. The forward-medium starter is an overhead.
The back-medium-punch or heavy-kick target continuation. Later target presses are not separate neutral links.
Stribog / Torbalan. Punch versus kick changes the special; OD versions use two buttons of the corresponding type.
Triglav with the listed punch strength. Placement matters; preserve the demonstrated spacing.
Departure portal placement / OD Embrace command grab. A later portal placement after knockdown is separate from the damage combo.
Forward medium kick overhead / forward heavy kick. Direction is relative to the opponent.
Two punches is Double Lariat; three punches is OD Double Lariat. They are different versions with different resource costs.
Down-forward medium punch. Keep it distinct from crouching medium punch.
Forward heavy punch. Its close-range link is separate from the forward heavy kick punish starter.
Full-circle command-throw notation. 360MP is medium Screw Piledriver; 720P is Level 3 Bolshoi Storm Buster.
The airborne OD command throw follows a launch. It is not a grounded Screw Piledriver.
Hold the punch button during Cyclone Lariat for the demonstrated launch; dash and juggle afterward.
Stored Wind stock; the enhanced Condor Spire variants shown consume one.
Mexican Typhoon command throw. The suffix specifies the demonstrated punch strength.
Raw Drive Rush costs one Drive bar; a normal cancelled into Drive Rush costs three.
Spiral Arrow / Cannon Spike / airborne Cannon Strike. Use the listed strength and grounded or airborne input.
Back medium punch into the heavy-kick target continuation. Follow the shown jump-cancel route when stated.
Standing heavy punch into its heavy-kick target continuation; distinct from Lift Combination.
Hold the heavy-special button for the demonstrated duration; exact timing follows the clip, not a new numeric frame claim.
The OD forward quarter-circle kick is Whirlwind Shot. Eagle Spike instead uses quarter-circle back plus kick.
Use the listed punch strength, then the separate Roll or Wing Stroke continuation.
Forward plus two kicks enters Run. This is different from a 66 forward dash.
Standing medium punch into heavy kick is the target sequence. Match its continuation timing.
The roll and subsequent kick are separate follow-up actions; keep both in the sequence.
A.K.I.’s poisoned-opponent routes have different properties. The creator marks poison-triggering attacks with an asterisk; references state the prerequisite explicitly.
214LP is the bubble. 6P is its separate Nightshade Chaser follow-up.
Light is horizontal, heavy rises upward. Match the listed version and the poison prerequisite.
2PP enters the slide stance; K performs Heel Strike. These are separate actions.
214HP is the close poison attack; 214MP places the poison pool. Pool placement after a combo is a setup, not a guaranteed later hit.
This 2023 recording has recipe overlays and poison effects but no input-history display. Routes are source-reviewed rather than current-patch tested.
Ed’s kick-button normals are performed as punches. Keep button labels distinct from the attack’s physical animation.
Standing MP into its HP target follow-up; a separate standing HP link is a different route.
Two kicks enters Kill Rush, called Kill Step in some source terminology.
Press forward plus punch late during forward Kill Rush. The early forward-punch continuation is Kill Switch Break, a different move.
Crouching medium punch is the low starter selected from the source’s “MK or 2MP” options. Crouching medium kick is a separate high-hitting button.
Use the listed strength. Knockdown setups preserve the source’s specific starter, ender, spacing and dated frame value.
Psycho Crusher requires back charge. Scissor Kicks uses a quarter-circle motion in SF6.
The strength matters. The selected initial routes start without a Psycho Mine and plant one with Backfist.
A planted mine changes later conversions. Do not substitute a mine-active route for a reference that begins without one.
Standing MP into forward HP is the target combo used after the blocked-DI wall splat.
Back heavy kick and standing heavy kick are different normals. Match the listed direction, especially in heavy links.
Power Charge uses a quarter-circle-forward motion. Its name does not mean holding a charge direction.
The heavy-punch wave is Round Wave, distinct from light Power Wave.
Crouching medium kick into its crouching-heavy-kick target follow-up. The follow-up is not a standalone sweep.
Wait for both heavy-punch hits where specified before canceling into the special.
SA2 starts Power Geyser. The first PP continuation is Twin Geyser and spends Drive; the second is Triple Geyser and spends an extra Super stock.
The heavy Crack Shoot juggle needs the demonstrated delay after Power Charge. Match height before the Rising Tackle finish.
An asterisk in the source denotes an enhanced special using Mai’s Flame stocks. Match each reference’s required stock state.
Perform the listed quarter-circle-back punch while airborne; the reference identifies a strength when the source establishes one.
A linked target-combo follow-up is a separate input. Match any standing-opponent condition in the reference.
Elena’s quarter-circle-forward kick special. Use the listed version and standing-opponent condition.
The quarter-circle-back kick entry has distinct follow-ups. The following direction and button identify the demonstrated branch.
A held heavy Tiger Uppercut is distinct from a tap; follow the listed hold cue.
Cancel the listed move into a High Jump with down then up. It spends one Drive bar outside the Limit Decoupler install; the airborne special is a separate input.
Cancel a Thunder Dash or Seismic Hammer startup using the kick input shown in the source. Feints are not landed special hits.
The forward + two-punch continuation after Thunder Dash is separate from the initial special and spends Drive.
Down + two punches enters Prowler Stance. Its follow-ups are separate inputs and differ from normal standing attacks.
Hold the listed heavy button for the charged version rather than tapping it. Match the reference’s starter and condition.
The source calls these Solar Crests; the official name is Sun Crests. Heavy and OD Sun Flare automatically spend up to two. A one-asterisk route requires exactly one starting Crest.
The second heavy punch after back heavy punch, or medium kick after medium punch, is a target-combo follow-up. Use the listed continuation.
An asterisk in the source denotes a Bayani-enhanced version. Match the stated Bayani condition before practising that route.
The forward-punch continuation is an input after the listed Daloy ng Tubig special; it is not a separate normal punch.
The forward-punch continuation belongs to the preceding Arm of Justice. It is a separate follow-up action, not a new normal attack.
An active Divine Pillar changes Cruel Shoulder into Justice Beyond. Match each route’s required pillar state.
